messages.author: d93038bd7441a9ea
messages.subject: Help!
parts:
Dear all!
We are trying to find the population density of an endemic species, the Cyprus moufflon.
We have our data separated in two strata; forest core and forest edge. The data was collected using 20 line transects and the perpendicular distance of the animals was estimated using a laser machine. Our problem is that we cannot find the correct density (the numbers are too low); the data is separated into region (forest core and forest edge), Line transect (label), Line transect (length), Observation (perpendicular distance) and 4 columns of observations (numbers of males, females, youngs and newborns). We use the uniform parameter with cosine adjustment (not sure if this is correct)

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: Help!
parts:
Hard to tell other than you need a single value which is the size of
each group. From your description it is most likely that the program is
estimating the number of groups rather than the number of critters.

Send the output if you want help with interpretation.

--jeff
